Cube v1.8.15 fails each query on a geo dimension of a view, also on the REST API: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'sql'). No map can work on a view. The driver hides this column and shows it as NULL, so the view stays usable. A map works on the cube of the dimension.

Cube Store puts a time before the origin of a custom granularity in months in the wrong bin, and no released Cube has a fix. The driver stops such a query when a rollup serves the measure and the data starts before the origin. An offset has its origin in the current year, so this stops most offsets on a rollup. A measure that no rollup serves gives the truth. An origin before all rows gives the truth on a rollup.

cube-clickhouse builds an original_sql pre-aggregation, and a query on the cube reads it. Its indexes have no effect. A rollup with use_original_sql_pre_aggregations still fails with Unknown table expression identifier, also with the dialect, so the query stops and no number is wrong.

Inside the range of the rollup, the lambda gives the truth. With a range that reads source rows on the demo data, the REST API and the SQL API of Cube can stop on ClickHouse with Stream query failed: aborted, see cube-js/cube#12285. A run gives the truth or this error. The driver shows a clear message for this. dev/cube/model/rollups.yml has the model.

Metabase has no column that lists the drill columns of a measure. Its drill-through uses all visible fields. The text in the description is the only place, see semantic.drill_members.

Known wrong number. The SQL API of Cube has the type Double for numbers, so a long decimal loses digits. Its value fits the range of a Double, so the driver cannot see this. SELECT dec_big FROM typed_events WHERE id = 3 gives 3000000000000 where the truth is 3000000000000.00000003. A dimension with SQL toString(column) keeps the digits, and the check proves this.

The check compares each card with SQL truth. A card that adds up a dimension of a joined cube (sum and avg of users.lifetime_orders) can stop. Stock Cube adds each row of the joined cube once. So it gives another number, and the driver stops this query with a clear message, see compile.join.total_of_dimension_refused. The check accepts this message or a number equal to the truth.

Cube with the Tesseract planner reads the first subquery for two sub_query dimensions with equal SQL when the query has a filter. The driver stops a query that groups by both, and raw rows show NULL in the later column. With other SQL, such as {orders.count} + 0, both work, and each is right alone, see dimension.opt.propagate_filters.

The driver does not use CUBEJS_SQL_SUPER_USER, SET user or __user. A live test on Cube v1.8.15 shows that a session of the super user accepts __user from native SQL, so a person who writes SQL reads as anybody. SET user works in one direction, so a pool cannot give the connection back. The driver connects as the person instead. See docs/security.md.
Limit of Cube: with CUBEJS_DEV_MODE=true the SQL API reads hidden cubes and members (m6). A Cube with dev mode off refuses this query. docs/security.md warns about it.
Limit of Metabase: this admin endpoint repeats the request body with the secret that the admin sent, for each driver (m7). No driver hook applies. Each read of a stored database gives the mask.
